newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver wedged in tight ranges.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver wedged in tight ranges.

text.p: The precious metals markets traded in tiny price ranges on Monday as the market searched for direction after gains from a modest rally eroded last week.
Bullion fixed virtually unchanged at $382.90 an ounce, versus $382.80 in the morning and $382.55 on Friday afternoon.
In New York's Comex futures market, December gold was unchanged at $384.60 an ounce.
Gold prices are expected to remain strangled within the broader $380-$385 price range until after the expiration of over-the-counter options on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The range is going to be $381.50 to $384.50 till after the expiry," one said. Options give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell gold at a given price at a future date.
Bullion fixed at $382.80 an ounce, compared to $382.55 an ounce on Friday afternoon.

Prices had edged up overnight on Chinese and Japanese buying, and demand for gold in India, the world's biggest consumer of the metal, has also picked up in recent days ahead of the upcoming Diwali festival of lights, analysts said.

But a statement from Portugal's economy minister that the country may sell some of its gold reserves injected a note of wariness into the market, although the Bank of Portugal governor has said he had no instructions to sell gold at this time.
"The statement has woken the market up a bit. The news isn't bearish because it's unsubstantiated but it takes out any bullish sentiment from the market," a dealer said.
The dollar's strength continued to dampen incentive to invest in gold, while the weakening South African rand would encourage gold producers to sell more metal, dealers said.

Silver was also static, indicated unchanged from Friday's close $4.91/$4.93 an ounce. Like gold, it was expected to stay within a tight range ahead of the options expiry, with the psychological $5.00 level capping attempts to move higher.
"It couldn't break through the well-defended $5.00 area last week, and on the downside support is at $4.85," a dealer said.
Platinum, which sank below the price of gold on Friday for the first time in three years was indicated barely higher from Friday's London close at $383.55/$384.55 an ounce, up $0.65.
Analysts said Friday's sell-off of platinum was due to the market being oversupplied and disillusioned, but it was finding support at current price levels.
Palladium was down 25 cents at $116.00/$117.00, heading back to recent lows after an attempt to edge towards $120 resistance last week fizzled out.
